reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right family (price, demand and close rate are unknowns a live sales test measures, $0 spend, bank-transfer settlement same day), but the plan as written cannot be let run. (1) The test takes paid orders before fulfilment is shown possible: the 'offer' step invoices $250 'paid before work starts' and the day-6 gate counts paid buyers, while Brain's FULFILMENT link is false ('nobody has established') and the card's fulfillment fact is only a RECOMMENDATION ('the owner, using AI-drafted copy'); nothing shows the owner can obtain manager access to a stranger's Google Business Profile and complete the listed scope (categories, services, description, captions, 10 scheduled posts, review-reply drafts) in 1.5 h within 48 h. (2) The proof gate passes at 1 paid of 80 by day 6, which does not carry the target: $1,000 / $250 = 4 sales, and the plan reaches only the same 80 businesses, so continuing on 1 of 80 (1.25%) projects ~$250, not $1,000; the threshold object (4 of 80) and the gate (1 of 80) disagree. (3) Owner hours do not fit the 5 h/week limit: week 1 (days 1-7) holds reach 2 h + sell 2 h + the first delivery 1.5 h on day 7 = 5.5 h; week 2 holds deliveries 2-4 (4.5 h) plus the continued replies/closes the 'continue' branch requires, which are not counted. (4) Price $250 is ASSUMED from a Bay Area agency list-rate roundup ($150-$800, basic SF setup ~$299) that I verified does not match this buyer population (research cnd_bacd16de88fd4c3abe29 was rejected by the gate); that is acceptable only as a price the test measures, which the plan should say. (5) members lists the resume and Upwork openings (7 and 10 deals) that the alternatives reject; the ledger should hold only the GBP opening.

reviews.reasons: All three MAJOR findings from my review of rev_592177c2ddf1_* are fixed, and the plan is a startable CONDITIONAL test with proof/stop/continue. (1) No buyer money is taken before fulfilment is shown: the offer is done-first and invoiced on delivery; the buyer adds the owner as a manager, which Google's help page (opened: 'you can invite users to become owners or managers'; managers have the same access except adding/removing users or removing the profile) supports; the first delivery is the timed fulfilment proof and the gate stops if it exceeds 1.5 h or access is refused. (2) The gate now carries the target at its threshold: 4 yeses of 80 (5%) x $250 = $1,000, threshold {4 of 80, reach 80} matches, below it the plan stops. (3) Owner hours recomputed: week 1 = reach 1 + sell 1 + first delivery 1.5 + second delivery 1.5 = 5 h <= 5; week 2 = sell 1 + 3 h deliveries = 4 h; total 9 h of the 10 allowed. Money: $0 spend, $0 exposure; receipts by Zelle/bank transfer on days 6, 8, 10, 12, all inside 14 days, ledger total $1,000 = target. Unknowns (close rate, price, demand, hours per delivery) are marked UNKNOWN/ASSUMED and are what the test decides; nothing unknown is treated as known. members now holds only the GBP opening.
findings: NOTE: The gate counts 'yeses', but cash arrives only on payment after delivery; with exactly 4 needed and invoicing after work, one non-payer leaves $750. Counting the first delivery's payment (as the proof does) helps; continuing to send beyond the 80 if a yes defaults would need hours that week 2 still has (1 h).

strategy.why: It needs $0 (cold email from the owner's own mailbox, Brain drafts the copy, buyer pays a bank-transfer/Zelle invoice so no new-processor hold), the published one-time price range is $150-$800 per location (basic ~$299), and 4 sales at $250 carry the $1,000. The close rate of cold-reached owners is unmeasured, so the plan starts as a time-boxed sales test inside the 14 days and 10 owner hours; the $250 price is itself measured by the test (the published $150-$800 range is a list-rate roundup that does not match this population).

alternatives.title: AI-assisted resume rewrite to job seekers via the owner's network
alternatives.why: Needs 7 buyers from a personal network nobody has measured; subcontracted writer cost is assumed, not established; weaker per-hour than GBP.

alternatives.title: Fixed-price blog articles on Upwork
alternatives.why: Client review window of up to 14 days plus a 5-day security hold makes settlement inside 14 days unlikely, and proposals cost Connects, which a $0 budget cannot fund.

steps.label: Brain lists 80 local businesses with visibly incomplete Google Business Profiles (public Google Maps) and drafts a personalised audit note and the full optimization copy for each

Offer: one-time GBP optimization for $250, done first and invoiced on delivery (pay by bank transfer/Zelle once the changes are live); the buyer adds the owner as a manager on the profile
Owner answers replies and takes yeses (Brain drafts every reply), week 1: 1h, week 2: 1h
evidence: close rate of cold-emailed local business owners

steps.label: Fulfilment proof: owner applies Brain's copy to the first yes's profile via manager access, timed; no invoice until it is live
Gate day 7: continue only if 4 of the 80 have said yes (5%, the rate that carries $1,000) and the first delivery took no more than 1.5h and was paid
evidence: close rate of cold-emailed local business owners

steps.label: Owner delivers the other 3 yeses (3 x 1.5h): 1.5h on day 7, 3h in week 2

review.reasons: All three MAJOR findings from my review of rev_592177c2ddf1_* are fixed, and the plan is a startable CONDITIONAL test with proof/stop/continue. (1) No buyer money is taken before fulfilment is shown: the offer is done-first and invoiced on delivery; the buyer adds the owner as a manager, which Google's help page (opened: 'you can invite users to become owners or managers'; managers have the same access except adding/removing users or removing the profile) supports; the first delivery is the timed fulfilment proof and the gate stops if it exceeds 1.5 h or access is refused. (2) The gate now carries the target at its threshold: 4 yeses of 80 (5%) x $250 = $1,000, threshold {4 of 80, reach 80} matches, below it the plan stops. (3) Owner hours recomputed: week 1 = reach 1 + sell 1 + first delivery 1.5 + second delivery 1.5 = 5 h <= 5; week 2 = sell 1 + 3 h deliveries = 4 h; total 9 h of the 10 allowed. Money: $0 spend, $0 exposure; receipts by Zelle/bank transfer on days 6, 8, 10, 12, all inside 14 days, ledger total $1,000 = target. Unknowns (close rate, price, demand, hours per delivery) are marked UNKNOWN/ASSUMED and are what the test decides; nothing unknown is treated as known. members now holds only the GBP opening.
findings: NOTE: The gate counts 'yeses', but cash arrives only on payment after delivery; with exactly 4 needed and invoicing after work, one non-payer leaves $750. Counting the first delivery's payment (as the proof does) helps; continuing to send beyond the 80 if a yes defaults would need hours that week 2 still has (1 h).
